chunks: Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Bundar, from Ahmad ibn Abu Abdullah, from one of the Iraqis, from Ibrahim ibn Uqba, from Ja'far al-Qalanisi, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), who said:

I said to him, 'We prepare the food, make it good, and are particular about it, but we do not find in it the aroma of the food of the wedding feast.' He said, 'That is because the food of the wedding feast has an aroma blowing from Paradise, because it is food prepared for the permissible (halal).'
ai.seo_question: Why does wedding food have a special aroma according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this narration from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) elucidates that the superior fragrance of wedding feast food stems from Paradise, attributing this spiritual quality to its preparation for halal purposes. This highlights the metaphysical dimension of sustenance in Shia tradition, where lawful consumption transforms physical nourishment into a conduit for divine blessing and sensory delight.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Muhammad Bin Bundar, from Ahmad Bin Abu Abdullah, from one of the Iraqis, from Ibrahim Bin Uqba, from Ja’far Al Qalanasy, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, ‘

I said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘We take the food, and we make it good, and are choosy in it, but we do not find for it the aroma of the food of the weddings’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘That is because the food of the wedding, in it is a gift of an aroma from the Paradise, because it is a meal taken for the Permissible’.
en.sarwar: 6. Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Bandar has narrated from Ahmad ibn abu ‘Abd Allah from certain persons of Iraq from Ibrahim ibn ‘Uqbah from Ja‘far al-Qalanisiy who has said the following:

“I once said to abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, ‘Why is it that we prepare good food and make it unique but we do not find the fragrance like that of the food for wedding in it?’ He (the Imam) said, ‘It is because in the food for wedding, air from paradise blows; it is a food that is prepared for a lawful matter (marriage).’ ”
